text: Experts have different opinions about the future of AI. Today we have "narrow AI", which can only do specific tasks, like translating languages or recognising faces. The next big step is "general AI" or AGI — a machine that can think and learn like a human across many different areas. Supporters say AGI could help solve serious problems, such as disease and climate change. However, critics warn about real risks, including job losses and safety concerns. Some researchers believe AGI may arrive within 20 years, while others think it is much further away. Nobody knows for sure, but most agree the choices we make now will shape what happens next.
